study_identification_part.si_4_title: Cortical thickness deviations as biomarker for subtyping and prognosis in pediatric brainstem tumors

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Data from 849 healthy children were sourced from four sources: (i) 61 locally recruited in Beijing; (ii) 69 from fcon_1000 projects dataset (FCON); (iii) 450 from the Child Connectome Project (devCCNP); (iv) 269 from the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center. Since 2 of 4 sources (Beijing local and Guangzhou hospital) do not match any named dataset in the reference list and the study uses multiple acquisition sites, MULTI-SITE (N>=2) is also applicable.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: To create a normative model, data from 849 healthy children were sourced from four databases: (i) 61 were locally recruited in Beijing; (ii) 69 from the fcon_1000 projects dataset; (iii) 450 from the Child Connectome Project (devCCNP); (iv) 269 from the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Jia2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Participants, L29

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All four healthy control datasets were combined and harmonized using ComBat, then used together to build a normative CTh model via 10-fold cross-validation. Patient data (145 pediatric brainstem tumor patients from Beijing Tiantan Hospital) were used to calculate CTh deviations from the normative model and for subtype classification.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Combat was used to harmonize MRI data across three datasets and address inter-scanner variability... We validated the models through 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy control dataset before finalizing the normative models. After that, these models were used to predict CTh for each participant and assess any deviations.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study built one normative model for CTh across 210 cerebral regions using GPR. The total healthy control sample was 849 children from 4 sources. Train/validation/test split was done via 10-fold cross-validation but specific numbers per fold are not reported.

It only states they are 'healthy children'. Patient age statistics are reported (mean=8.4, SD=3.4, median=8.0), but healthy control age distributions are not provided in the main text or supplementary materials.
